questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of demand?
options: The quantity customers are willing and able to buy at a given price over a period of time
The quantity of a good that producers offer for sale at a given price
The total number of people living in a market
The amount customers would like to own regardless of price
questions.why: Demand requires both willingness and ability to pay, and it is always at a stated price over a stated period. Wanting something you cannot afford is not demand.
whyNot: That is the definition of supply. Demand comes from buyers, supply from sellers.
Population affects demand but is not demand itself. A large population with no spending power generates little demand.
This leaves out both price and ability to pay, which are the two things that make it demand rather than a wish.

questions.stem: The price of a product falls and more of it is bought. This is best described as:
options: a movement along the demand curve
a shift of the demand curve to the right
a shift of the demand curve to the left
an increase in supply
questions.why: A change in the price of the good itself moves you along the existing demand curve. The curve does not move. This distinction is the most heavily tested idea in the topic.
whyNot: A shift right means more is demanded at every price, caused by something other than the good's own price. Here it was the price that changed.
A shift left means less is demanded at every price. Neither shift applies to a change in the good's own price.
Nothing here says anything about producers' willingness to supply.

questions.stem: Which term is defined as: a change in the quantity demanded at every price, caused by a factor other than the price of the good itself?
options: A shift in the demand curve
A movement along the demand curve
Price elasticity of demand
An equilibrium
questions.why: A shift is a change in demand at every price. It is caused by the non-price factors: substitutes and complements, incomes, tastes, marketing, demographics, shocks and seasonality.
whyNot: A movement is caused only by a change in the good's own price, and happens along the existing curve.
PED measures how responsive quantity demanded is to a price change. It describes the steepness of a curve, not a shift of it.
An equilibrium is where supply meets demand. It is a point, not a change.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of a complementary good?
options: A good bought alongside another, so a fall in the price of one increases demand for the other
A good bought instead of another, so a fall in the price of one reduces demand for the other
A good given away free with a purchase
A good whose demand falls as income rises
questions.why: Complements are used together, such as phones and data plans. Cheaper phones means more phones sold, which increases demand for data plans, shifting that curve right.
whyNot: That is a substitute. Substitutes are alternatives; complements are companions.
That is a free gift or promotional offer. The word complementary here means used together, not given free.
That is an inferior good, which is about income rather than about another good's price.

questions.stem: The price of tea falls sharply. What is the most likely effect on the demand curve for coffee?
options: It shifts to the left
It shifts to the right
There is a movement along it
It becomes perfectly inelastic
questions.why: Tea is a substitute for coffee. Cheaper tea causes some customers to switch away from coffee, so less coffee is demanded at every price and the coffee demand curve shifts left.
whyNot: A shift right would happen if a complement to coffee got cheaper, or if coffee became more fashionable. A cheaper substitute reduces demand.
A movement along the coffee curve needs a change in the price of coffee itself. Here it is the price of tea that changed.
A price change in a substitute shifts the curve. It does not make demand completely unresponsive to price.

questions.stem: Which of the following would shift the demand curve for a normal good to the right?
options: An increase in consumer incomes
A fall in the price of the good itself
An increase in the cost of raw materials
The introduction of an indirect tax on the good
questions.why: For a normal good, higher incomes mean more is demanded at every price, so the whole curve shifts right.
whyNot: A change in the good's own price causes a movement along the curve, not a shift of it.
Raw material costs affect the producer's willingness to supply. They shift the supply curve, not demand.
An indirect tax also acts on the supply side, shifting supply left and raising the equilibrium price.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of seasonality?
options: A regular, predictable pattern in demand that repeats at the same points each year
An unexpected event outside the business's control that changes demand
A long-term change in the age structure of a population
A permanent decline in demand for a product
questions.why: Seasonality repeats to a timetable, which is what makes it manageable. Because it is predictable it counts as a risk rather than an uncertainty, and businesses plan staffing, stock and pricing around it.
whyNot: That is an external shock. The key difference is that a shock cannot be predicted, so it cannot be planned for.
That is demographic change, which is gradual and long-term rather than repeating annually.
A permanent decline is a structural change in the market. Seasonality always reverses.

questions.stem: A resort's bookings fall every year during the wet season and recover every dry season. How should the business treat this?
options: As a risk, because it is predictable and can be planned for
As an uncertainty, because demand is falling
As an external shock, because the weather is outside its control
As a permanent shift left in its demand curve
questions.why: The pattern repeats every year, so a probability can be attached to it from past data. That makes it risk, and it can be managed with seasonal contracts, off-peak pricing and scheduled maintenance.
whyNot: Uncertainty means no probability can be attached. A pattern that repeats annually is the opposite of that.
Being outside the firm's control is not enough to make something a shock. A shock must also be unpredictable, and the monsoon is not.
A permanent shift would not reverse. This one reverses every year.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of demand changing because of demographics?
options: Demand for elderly care services rising as the population ages
Demand for umbrellas rising during the rainy season
Demand for a product rising after a successful advertising campaign
Demand for a product falling after its price is increased
questions.why: Demographics are the measurable characteristics of a population, such as its age structure. An ageing population shifts demand towards healthcare and away from products for the young.
whyNot: That is seasonality, a repeating annual pattern rather than a change in the population.
That is marketing and advertising, which is the one shifter the business directly controls.
That is a movement along the demand curve, caused by the good's own price.

questions.stem: Which of these is the strongest reason why an advertising campaign that shifts demand right may still leave a business worse off?
options: The campaign may cost more than the extra profit the additional demand generates
Advertising always makes demand more price elastic
Shifting demand right lowers the price the business can charge
A shift right reduces the quantity demanded at every price
questions.why: Advertising is a cost. If the campaign costs $50,000 and the extra sales generate $30,000 of additional profit, the curve has shifted right and the business has still lost $20,000. Weighing the cost against the gain is what earns evaluation marks.
whyNot: Successful advertising usually makes demand *less* elastic, because loyal customers are less willing to switch on price.
A rightward shift in demand tends to allow a higher price, not a lower one, since more is demanded at every price.
A shift right means *more* is demanded at every price. A leftward shift reduces it.

questions.stem: For an inferior good, an increase in consumer incomes will:
options: shift the demand curve to the left
shift the demand curve to the right
cause a movement along the demand curve
leave demand completely unchanged
questions.why: An inferior good is one customers abandon as they get richer, trading up to something better. So higher incomes mean less is demanded at every price, and the curve shifts left.
whyNot: That is what happens to a normal good. The whole point of an inferior good is that it behaves the opposite way.
A movement requires a change in the good's own price. Income is a non-price factor, so it shifts the curve.
Income does affect demand for an inferior good, just in the opposite direction to a normal good.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of an external shock?
options: An unexpected event outside the control of a business that changes demand or supply
A predictable annual change in demand
A decision by a competitor to lower its price
A change in the price of the business's own product
questions.why: A shock is both outside the firm's control and unforeseeable, such as a pandemic, a war or a sudden currency collapse. Because no probability can be attached, it is uncertainty rather than risk.
whyNot: That is seasonality, which is predictable and therefore manageable.
A competitor cutting price is a normal feature of a competitive market and is broadly foreseeable, not a shock in this sense.
That is under the business's own control and causes a movement along its demand curve.

questions.stem: Which sentence would earn the most credit when describing an increase in demand in an exam answer?
options: The demand curve shifts to the right, so more is demanded at every price
Demand goes up
The demand curve moves up the graph
The quantity demanded increases because the price fell
questions.why: It names the direction of the shift and states what the shift actually means. That precision is what distinguishes an answer that earns the mark from one that does not.
whyNot: Too vague. It does not say whether the curve shifted or you moved along it, which is exactly what the examiner is checking.
For demand, an increase is described as a shift to the right. Saying up is imprecise and can suggest a price change instead.
This describes a movement along the curve caused by a price fall, which is a different thing from an increase in demand.

questions.stem: Why is demographic change the easiest of the demand shifters for a business to plan for?
options: It happens slowly and is highly predictable
It only ever increases demand
It is fully under the business's control
It does not affect the demand curve
questions.why: Population structures change over decades and are measured continuously, so a business can see an ageing population or rapid urbanisation coming years ahead and invest accordingly.
whyNot: It can shift demand either way: an ageing population raises demand for healthcare and lowers it for baby products.
A business cannot influence a country's population structure. It is predictable, not controllable.
Demographics are one of the listed shifters and do move the curve.

questions.stem: Incomes in a region rise by 6% and a business's product is a normal good. Which chain of reasoning is most complete?
options: Incomes rise, the good is normal, so demand shifts right and more is demanded at every price, allowing a higher price or greater volume, raising revenue provided the business has the capacity to supply it
Incomes rise, so demand rises and revenue rises
Incomes rise, so the business should raise its price
Incomes rise, so the demand curve moves along to a new point
questions.why: It identifies the cause, classifies the good, names the shift and what it means, states what the business can do, and then adds the condition it depends on. That is the structure of a full-mark analysis answer.
whyNot: Only two links, with no mention of the shift, what it means, or any condition. It would earn a low analysis mark.
It jumps straight to a recommendation with no reasoning in between, and ignores whether demand or capacity supports it.
Wrong mechanism. Income is a non-price factor, so the curve shifts rather than you moving along it.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of goods are substitutes?
options: Two competing brands of bottled water
Printers and printer ink
Cars and petrol
Cameras and memory cards
questions.why: Substitutes are alternatives that satisfy the same need, so a customer buys one instead of the other. A price cut by one brand of bottled water shifts demand for the rival brand left.
whyNot: These are complements, bought and used together. Cheaper printers increase demand for ink.
Complements. You cannot use the car without the fuel, so their demands move together.
Complements. A memory card is bought to be used with the camera, not instead of it.
